# Example Org — Secure Development Lifecycle Standard

**Document Owner:** Application Security
**Cadence:** Continuous
**Status:** Approved

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for acquiring, developing, and managing systems at Example Org using a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) that incorporates information security and privacy considerations. [NIST 800-53 SA-3 | ARC-AMPE SA-3]

The Application Security team is accountable for this process end to end. Application Security performs, reviews, and answers for each step in this document, including all handoffs between participating teams. This Standard applies to all systems, components, and services developed internally or acquired from developers, vendors, or service providers, throughout development, implementation, operation, and disposal.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities

Application Security shall define and document information security and privacy roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle, and shall identify the individuals holding those roles. [NIST 800-53 SA-3 | ARC-AMPE SA-3]

Application Security shall integrate the organizational information security and privacy risk management process into system development life cycle activities. [NIST 800-53 SA-3 | ARC-AMPE SA-3]

Security and privacy offices must have an opportunity to ensure that requirements to protect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) are appropriately considered throughout the system development life cycle. [ARC-AMPE SA-3]

## 3. System Development Life Cycle Controls

### 3.1 Preproduction Environments

Application Security shall protect system preproduction environments commensurate with risk throughout the system development life cycle. [NIST 800-53 SA-3(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-3(1)]

Application Security shall approve, document, and control the use of live data in preproduction environments. [NIST 800-53 SA-3(2) | ARC-AMPE SA-3(2)]

Application Security shall protect preproduction environments at the same impact or classification level as any live data in use within them. [NIST 800-53 SA-3(2) | ARC-AMPE SA-3(2)]

If PII is used in the test environment, the same controls required for systems containing PII must be applied to the test environment, and synthetic PII must be used to the maximum extent practicable when testing system functionality. [ARC-AMPE SA-3(2)]

The creation, collection, use, and/or disclosure of PII must be limited only to the extent necessary to accomplish a specified and authorized purpose. [ARC-AMPE SA-3(2)]

The senior official for privacy must approve the use of PII in testing, training, and research; synthetic or de-identified data is preferred for these purposes. [ARC-AMPE SA-3(2)]

### 3.2 Technology Refresh

Application Security shall plan for and implement a technology refresh schedule for the system throughout the system development life cycle. [NIST 800-53 SA-3(3)]

## 4. Acquisition and Contracting

### 4.1 Contract Content

Application Security shall ensure that the acquisition contract for the system, component, or service includes, explicitly or by reference, using standardized contract language:

- security and privacy functional requirements;
- strength of mechanism requirements;
- security and privacy assurance requirements;
- controls needed to satisfy security and privacy requirements;
- security and privacy documentation requirements;
- requirements for protecting that documentation;
- a description of the development environment and intended operating environment;
- allocation of responsibility (or identification of responsible parties) for information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management; and
- acceptance criteria. [NIST 800-53 SA-4 | ARC-AMPE SA-4]

Each contract and Statement of Work involving development of, or access to, systems containing PII must include language requiring adherence to the organization's security and privacy policies and standards (consistent with 45 CFR §155.260(b)), define security and privacy roles and responsibilities, and receive approval from the system owner. [ARC-AMPE SA-4]

When acquiring systems, components, or services used to store, process, or transmit PII, Application Security must include in the acquisition contract, in consultation with the privacy office: a list of security and privacy controls necessary to protect PII (and, if appropriate, enforce applicable privacy requirements); privacy requirements including privacy training and awareness and rules of behavior; and privacy functional requirements. [ARC-AMPE SA-4]

Application Security shall include organization-defined Privacy Act requirements in the acquisition contract for the operation of a system of records on behalf of the organization. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(11)]

Application Security shall include organizational data ownership requirements in the acquisition contract, and must require all data to be removed from the contractor's system and returned to the organization within an organization-defined time frame. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(12)]

### 4.2 Business Associate Requirements for Protected Health Information

A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf only if it obtains satisfactory assurances (in accordance with § 164.314(a)) that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information; a business associate must obtain the same satisfactory assurances from any subcontractor before permitting it to handle electronic protected health information on its behalf. [HIPAA 164.308(b)(1)]

The required satisfactory assurances must be documented through a written contract or other arrangement with the business associate that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a). [HIPAA 164.308(b)(3) Required]

The business associate contract must provide that the business associate will comply with the applicable requirements of the subpart, ensure that any subcontractors creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting electronic protected health information on its behalf agree to comply via a compliant contract or other arrangement, and report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410. [HIPAA 164.314(a)(2)(i) Required]

The requirements applicable to business associate contracts apply in the same manner to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and its subcontractor. [HIPAA 164.314(a)(2)(iii) Required]

### 4.3 Developer Deliverables and Evidence

Application Security shall require the developer to provide a description of the functional properties of the security and privacy controls to be implemented. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-4(1)]

Application Security shall require the developer to provide design and implementation information for the controls — including security-relevant external system interfaces, high-level design documentation, and source code or hardware schematics — at an organization-defined level of detail sufficient to prove control implementation. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(2) | ARC-AMPE SA-4(2)]

Functional properties of security controls describe only the functionality visible at the interfaces of the controls and specifically exclude functionality and data structures internal to the operation of the controls. [ARC-AMPE SA-4(2)]

Application Security shall require the developer to follow organization-defined systems engineering methods, security and/or privacy engineering methods, software development methods, testing/evaluation/verification/validation methods, and quality control processes. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(3)]

Application Security shall require the system, component, or service to be delivered with organization-defined security configurations implemented, and shall require those configurations to be used as the default for any subsequent reinstallation or upgrade. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(5) High]

### 4.4 Product Selection Restrictions

Application Security shall employ only government off-the-shelf or commercial off-the-shelf information assurance (and IA-enabled) products that compose an NSA-approved solution to protect classified information transmitted over networks at a lower classification level, and shall ensure those products have been evaluated and/or validated by NSA or in accordance with NSA-approved procedures. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(6)]

Application Security shall limit the use of commercially provided information assurance products to those successfully evaluated against a NIAP-approved Protection Profile for the technology type (if one exists); if no such profile exists but the product relies on cryptographic functionality to enforce its security policy, Application Security must require that the cryptographic module is FIPS-validated or NSA-approved. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(7)]

Application Security shall employ only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(10)]

### 4.5 Continuous Monitoring and Operational Requirements

Application Security shall require the developer to produce a plan for continuous monitoring of control effectiveness that is consistent with the organization's continuous monitoring program. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(8)]

Application Security shall require the developer to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for organizational use. [NIST 800-53 SA-4(9) | ARC-AMPE SA-4(9)]

## 5. System Documentation

### 5.1 Administrator and User Documentation

Application Security shall obtain or develop administrator documentation describing the secure configuration, installation, and operation of the system, component, or service; the effective use and maintenance of security and privacy functions and mechanisms; and known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative or privileged functions. [NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall obtain or develop user documentation describing user-accessible security and privacy functions and how to use them effectively; methods for user interaction that enable more secure use and protect individual privacy; and user responsibilities for maintaining system security and individual privacy. [NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall document attempts to obtain system documentation when it is unavailable or nonexistent, and shall take organization-defined actions in response. [NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall distribute documentation to organization-defined personnel or roles. [NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall follow the FedRAMP Secure Configuration Guide rules. [FedRAMP SA-5]

### 5.2 Documentation Lifecycle

Application Security shall develop system documentation that describes the system and specifies its purpose, technical operation, access, maintenance, and required training for administrators and users. [ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall maintain an updated list of related system operations and security documentation. [ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Upon changes in system functions or processes, Application Security shall update the relevant system documentation and shall ensure the documents include date and version numbers. [ARC-AMPE SA-5]

Application Security shall evaluate and protect documentation based on whether it aligns with the risk management strategy or is essential for the effective implementation or operation of security controls. [ARC-AMPE SA-5]

## 6. Security and Privacy Engineering Principles

Application Security shall apply organization-defined systems security and privacy engineering principles in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system and system components. [NIST 800-53 SA-8 | ARC-AMPE SA-8]

Application Security shall implement the following NIST-defined security design principles in organization-defined systems or system components as applicable: [NIST 800-53 SA-8(1)–SA-8(32)]

- clear abstractions
- least common mechanism
- modularity and layering
- partially ordered dependencies
- efficiently mediated access
- minimized sharing
- reduced complexity
- secure evolvability
- trusted components
- hierarchical trust
- inverse modification threshold
- hierarchical protection
- minimized security elements
- least privilege
- predicate permission
- self-reliant trustworthiness
- secure distributed composition
- trusted communications channels
- continuous protection
- secure metadata management
- self-analysis
- accountability and traceability
- secure defaults
- secure failure and recovery
- economic security
- performance security
- human factored security
- acceptable security
- repeatable and documented procedures
- procedural rigor
- secure system modification
- sufficient documentation

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of least privilege in organization-defined systems or system components, consistent with the principle of least privilege as discussed in AC-6 and reflected in all aspects of secure system design. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(14) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(14)]

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of trusted communications channels in organization-defined systems or system components, including restricting access to the communication channel and employing end-to-end protections for data transmitted over it. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(18) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(18)]

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of accountability and traceability in organization-defined systems or system components, tracing security-relevant actions (subject-object interactions) to the entity on whose behalf the action is taken and creating a trustworthy infrastructure that records details of actions affecting system security. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(22) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(22)]

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of secure defaults in organization-defined systems or system components. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(23) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(23)]

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of secure system modification in organization-defined systems or system components; all system changes must be accompanied by a Security Impact Analysis (SIA) and a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA). [NIST 800-53 SA-8(31) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(31)]

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of sufficient documentation in organization-defined systems or system components. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(32) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(32)]

Application Security shall implement the privacy principle of minimization using organization-defined processes, driven by business needs, coordinated with the senior privacy officer, and consistent with PM-25, PT-2, and SI-12. [NIST 800-53 SA-8(33) | ARC-AMPE SA-8(33)]

## 7. Developer Configuration Management

Application Security shall require the developer to perform configuration management during system, component, or service design, development, implementation, operation, and disposal. [NIST 800-53 SA-10 | ARC-AMPE SA-10]

Application Security shall require the developer to document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to organization-defined configuration items. [NIST 800-53 SA-10 | ARC-AMPE SA-10]

Application Security shall require the developer to implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service. [NIST 800-53 SA-10 | ARC-AMPE SA-10]

Application Security shall require the developer to document approved changes and the potential security and privacy impacts of those changes. [NIST 800-53 SA-10 | ARC-AMPE SA-10]

Application Security shall require the developer to track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and to report findings to organization-defined personnel or roles. [NIST 800-53 SA-10 | ARC-AMPE SA-10]

Application Security shall require the developer to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-10(1)]

Application Security shall provide an alternate configuration management process using organizational personnel in the absence of a dedicated developer configuration management team. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(2)]

Application Security shall require the developer to enable integrity verification of hardware components. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(3)]

Application Security shall require the developer to employ tools for comparing newly generated versions of security-relevant hardware descriptions, source code, and object code with previous versions. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(4)]

Application Security shall require the developer to maintain the integrity of the mapping between the master build data for the current version of security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and the on-site master copy of that data. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(5)]

Application Security shall require the developer to execute procedures ensuring that security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware updates distributed to the organization are exactly as specified by the master copies. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(6)]

Application Security shall require organization-defined security and privacy representatives to be included in the organization-defined configuration change management and control process. [NIST 800-53 SA-10(7)]

## 8. Developer Security Testing and Evaluation

### 8.1 Assessment Planning and Execution

Application Security shall require the developer, at all post-design stages of the system development life cycle, to develop and implement a plan for ongoing security and privacy control assessments. [NIST 800-53 SA-11 | ARC-AMPE SA-11]

Application Security shall require the developer to perform unit, integration, system, and regression testing/evaluation at an organization-defined frequency, depth, and coverage. [NIST 800-53 SA-11 | ARC-AMPE SA-11]

Application Security shall require the developer to produce evidence of the execution of the assessment plan and the results of the testing and evaluation. [NIST 800-53 SA-11 | ARC-AMPE SA-11]

Application Security shall require the developer to implement a verifiable flaw remediation process. [NIST 800-53 SA-11 | ARC-AMPE SA-11]

Application Security shall require the developer to correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation. [NIST 800-53 SA-11 | ARC-AMPE SA-11]

No security-relevant modifications of the information systems should be made after the assessment. [ARC-AMPE SA-11]

Application Security shall require the developer to verify that the scope of testing and evaluation provides complete coverage of the required controls at the organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and evaluation. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(7)]

### 8.2 Test Environment Isolation

Non-production data must be used when executing test scripts or in a test environment that is configured to comply with the security controls as though it were a production environment. [ARC-AMPE SA-11]

All systems supporting development and pre-production testing must be connected to an isolated network separated from production systems; network traffic into and out of that environment must be permitted only to facilitate system testing, restricted by source and destination access control lists as well as ports and protocols. [ARC-AMPE SA-11]

### 8.3 Analysis and Testing Techniques

Application Security shall require the developer to employ static code analysis tools to identify common flaws and to document the results of the analysis. Static analysis (SAST) results shall be produced per release and retained as evidence. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(1) | ARC-AMPE SA-11(1)]

Application Security shall require the developer to perform threat modeling and vulnerability analyses during development and subsequent testing and evaluation, using organization-defined contextual information (impact, environment of operations, known or assumed threats, and acceptable risk levels), organization-defined tools and methods, at an organization-defined breadth and depth of modeling and analyses, producing evidence that meets organization-defined acceptance criteria. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(2) | ARC-AMPE SA-11(2)]

Application Security shall require an independent agent satisfying organization-defined independence criteria to verify correct implementation of the developer's security and privacy assessment plans and the evidence produced during testing and evaluation, and shall verify the agent is provided with sufficient information or granted the authority to obtain it. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(3)]

Application Security shall require the developer to perform a manual code review of organization-defined specific code using organization-defined processes, procedures, and/or techniques. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(4)]

Application Security shall require the developer to perform penetration testing at an organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and under organization-defined constraints. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(5)]

Application Security shall require the developer to perform attack surface reviews. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(6)]

Application Security shall require the developer to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify common flaws and to document the results of the analysis. Dynamic analysis (DAST) results shall be produced per release and retained as evidence. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(8) | ARC-AMPE SA-11(8)]

Application Security shall require the developer to employ interactive application security testing tools to identify flaws and document the results. [NIST 800-53 SA-11(9)]

## 9. Development Process, Standards, and Tools

Application Security shall require the developer to follow a documented development process that explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements, identifies the standards and tools used, documents the specific tool options and tool configurations used, and documents, manages, and ensures the integrity of changes to the process and/or tools used in development. [NIST 800-53 SA-15 | ARC-AMPE SA-15]

Application Security shall review the development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations at least every one (1) year or as needed to determine whether they can satisfy organization-defined security and privacy requirements. [NIST 800-53 SA-15 | ARC-AMPE SA-15]

The organization-defined security and privacy requirements for the development process must be based on the ARC-AMPE security and privacy controls or their equivalent, and must include all applicable System Acquisition (SA) and Configuration Management (CM) security controls. [ARC-AMPE SA-15]

Application Security shall require the developer to minimize the use of personally identifiable information in development and test environments. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(12) | NIST 800-53 SA-15(13) | ARC-AMPE SA-15(12)]

### 9.1 Development Process Enhancements

Application Security shall define quality metrics at the beginning of the development process and shall require evidence of meeting them at an organization-defined frequency, program review, and/or upon delivery. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(1)]

Application Security shall require the developer to select and employ security and privacy tracking tools for use during the development process. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(2)]

Application Security shall perform criticality analysis at organization-defined decision points in the system development life cycle and at an organization-defined breadth and depth of analysis. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(3) Moderate, High]

Application Security shall require the developer to reduce attack surfaces to organization-defined thresholds. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(5)]

Application Security shall require the developer to implement an explicit process to continuously improve the development process. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(6)]

Application Security shall perform automated vulnerability analysis using organization-defined tools; shall determine the exploitation potential and potential risk mitigations for discovered vulnerabilities; and shall deliver the tool outputs and analysis results to organization-defined personnel or roles. Dependency and supply-chain scan output shall be produced per release and retained as evidence. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(7)]

Application Security shall require the developer to use threat modeling and vulnerability analyses from similar systems, components, or services to inform the current development process. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(8)]

Application Security shall require the developer to provide, implement, and test an incident response plan. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(10)]

Application Security shall require the developer to archive the system or component to be released or delivered together with the corresponding evidence supporting the final security and privacy review. [NIST 800-53 SA-15(11)]

## 10. Developer Training and Architecture

### 10.1 Developer Security Training

Application Security shall require the developer to provide organization-defined training on the correct use and operation of the implemented security and privacy functions, controls, and/or mechanisms. [NIST 800-53 SA-16 High]

### 10.2 Security and Privacy Architecture

Application Security shall require the developer to produce a design specification and security and privacy architecture that is consistent with the organization's security and privacy architecture (an integral part of the enterprise architecture), accurately and completely describes the required security and privacy functionality and the allocation of controls among physical and logical components, and expresses how individual security and privacy functions, mechanisms, and services work together to provide the required capabilities and a unified approach to protection. [NIST 800-53 SA-17 | ARC-AMPE SA-17]

Application Security shall produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal policy model describing the organization-defined elements of organizational security and privacy policy to be enforced, and shall prove the model is internally consistent and sufficient to enforce those elements when implemented. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(1)]

Application Security shall define security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and shall provide a rationale that the definition is complete. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(2)]

Application Security shall produce a formal top-level specification specifying the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; shall demonstrate its consistency with the formal policy model, its complete coverage of those interfaces, and its accuracy as a description of the implemented components; and shall describe security-relevant mechanisms strictly internal to those components not addressed in the specification. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(3)]

Application Security shall produce an informal descriptive top-level specification specifying the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; shall demonstrate its consistency with the formal policy model, its complete coverage of those interfaces, and its accuracy; and shall describe security-relevant internal mechanisms not addressed in the specification. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(4)]

Application Security shall design and structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to use a complete, conceptually simple protection mechanism with precisely defined semantics, and shall internally structure those components with specific regard for this mechanism. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(5)]

Application Security shall require the developer to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate testing. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(6)]

Application Security shall require the developer to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate controlling access with least privilege. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(7)]

Application Security shall design organization-defined critical systems with coordinated behavior to implement organization-defined capabilities. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(8)]

Application Security shall use different designs for organization-defined critical systems to satisfy a common set of requirements or to provide equivalent functionality. [NIST 800-53 SA-17(9)]

## 11. Developer Personnel and Unsupported Components

### 11.1 Developer Personnel Screening

Application Security shall require that the developer of systems, components, or services has appropriate access authorizations as determined by the assigned Authorizing Official (or designee) and satisfies personnel screening criteria consistent with PS-3. [NIST 800-53 SA-21 High | ARC-AMPE SA-21]

### 11.2 Unsupported Components

Application Security shall replace system components when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer. [NIST 800-53 SA-22 | ARC-AMPE SA-22]

Application Security shall provide alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components, such as in-house support or support from organization-defined external providers. [NIST 800-53 SA-22]

Where unsupported components are retained to satisfy mission/business needs, Application Security shall document the justification and approval in a risk acceptance form and shall update the related Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) finding. [ARC-AMPE SA-22]

Application Security shall establish plans to mitigate or remove unsupported systems, applications, operating systems, or software once identified, and shall upgrade, retire, or stop use of the component before end of life or vendor discontinuation of product support. [ARC-AMPE SA-22]

If removal is not feasible, Application Security shall maintain a governance process to review unsupported system components and make a risk-based decision on their continued use. [ARC-AMPE SA-22]

## 12. Input Validation and Error Handling

### 12.1 Input Validation

Application Security shall ensure the validity of all information inputs to web/application servers, database servers, and any system or application input that might receive a crafted exploit toward executing code or causing a buffer overflow, verifying that inputs match specified definitions for format and content. [NIST 800-53 SI-10 | ARC-AMPE SI-10]

When PII is entered, validation techniques that support data quality must be used (e.g., ensuring the PII entered is the expected type and format), and the system must provide the capability to limit or exclude entering PII in fields that should not contain it; reasonable steps must be taken to ensure PII is complete, accurate, and up to date as required by laws and regulations. [ARC-AMPE SI-10]

Application Security shall provide a manual override capability for input validation of organization-defined information inputs, shall restrict its use to organization-defined authorized individuals, and shall audit its use. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(1)]

Application Security shall review and resolve input validation errors within an organization-defined time period. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(2)]

Application Security shall verify that the system behaves in a predictable and documented manner when invalid inputs are received. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(3)]

Application Security shall account for timing interactions among system components in determining appropriate responses for invalid inputs. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(4)]

Application Security shall restrict the use of information inputs to organization-defined trusted sources and/or organization-defined formats. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(5)]

Application Security shall prevent untrusted data injections. [NIST 800-53 SI-10(6)]

### 12.2 Error Messages

Application Security shall generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited — such as user name and password combinations, password-reset validation attributes, PII, biometric or authentication data, sensitive financial records, or content related to internal security functions. [NIST 800-53 SI-11 | ARC-AMPE SI-11]

Application Security shall reveal error messages only to organization-defined personnel or roles (documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan) — authorized individuals with a need for the information in the performance of their duties. [NIST 800-53 SI-11 | ARC-AMPE SI-11]

## 13. Supply Chain Risk Management

### 13.1 Supply Chain Risk Process

Application Security shall establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of organization-defined systems or components, in coordination with organization-defined supply chain personnel. [NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3]

Application Security shall employ organization-defined supply chain controls to protect against supply chain risks to the system, component, or service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chain-related events; these controls are not limited to those defined in ARC-AMPE and may include other NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supply chain controls as appropriate. [NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3]

Application Security shall document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in security and privacy plans, the supply chain risk management plan, and any other organization-defined document. [NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3]

The Chief Security Officer (CSO) must document and maintain supply chain custody, including replacement devices, to ensure the integrity of devices before they are introduced to the boundary. [FedRAMP SR-3]

Application Security shall employ a diverse set of sources for organization-defined system components and services. [NIST 800-53 SR-3(1)]

Application Security shall employ organization-defined controls to limit harm from potential adversaries identifying and targeting the organizational supply chain. [NIST 800-53 SR-3(2)]

Application Security shall ensure that the controls included in the contracts of prime contractors are also included in the contracts of subcontractors. [NIST 800-53 SR-3(3)]

Application Security shall employ organization-defined acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks. [NIST 800-53 SR-5]

Application Security shall employ organization-defined controls to ensure an adequate supply of organization-defined critical system components. [NIST 800-53 SR-5(1)]

Application Security shall assess the system, component, or service prior to selection, acceptance, modification, or update. [NIST 800-53 SR-5(2)]

### 13.2 Tamper Protection and Counterfeit Components

Application Security shall implement a tamper protection program for the system, component, or service. [NIST 800-53 SR-9 High]

Application Security shall employ anti-tamper technologies, tools, and techniques throughout the system development life cycle. [NIST 800-53 SR-9(1) High]

Application Security shall inspect organization-defined systems or system components (at random, at an organization-defined frequency, and/or upon organization-defined indications of need for inspection) to detect tampering. [NIST 800-53 SR-10]

Application Security shall develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system. [NIST 800-53 SR-11]

Application Security shall report counterfeit system components to the source of the counterfeit component, organization-defined external reporting organizations, and/or organization-defined personnel or roles. [NIST 800-53 SR-11]

Application Security shall train organization-defined personnel or roles to detect counterfeit system components (including hardware, software, and firmware). [NIST 800-53 SR-11(1)]

Application Security shall maintain configuration control over organization-defined system components awaiting service or repair and serviced or repaired components awaiting return to service. [NIST 800-53 SR-11(2)]

Application Security shall scan for counterfeit system components at an organization-defined frequency. [NIST 800-53 SR-11(3)]

### 13.3 Disposal

Application Security shall dispose of organization-defined data, documentation, tools, or system components using techniques and methods in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization, consistent with MP-6 Media Sanitization. [NIST 800-53 SR-12 | ARC-AMPE SR-12]

## 14. Evidence and Recordkeeping

The Application Security team shall retain, on a continuous basis, the following evidence artifacts demonstrating execution of this Standard:

| Artifact                                | Produced By          | Associated Controls |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- |
| SAST results per release                | Application Security | SA-11(1)            |
| DAST results per release                | Application Security | SA-11(8)            |
| Dependency and supply-chain scan output | Application Security | SA-15(7), SR-3      |

Application Security is responsible for the completeness and retention of these artifacts and shall make them available for audit and assessment activities.
